conventions.commits: Conventional commits with a type(scope) prefix (for example feat(core): add Swift language support with tree-sitter-swift handler (#1742)); each commit carries Signed-off-by (DCO) trailers; recent main commits carry a GPG signature (git %G? returns E in this clone, so verification is not possible here). CI runs a lint-commits job.
conventions.testing: Unit tests live in #[cfg(test)] mod tests at the bottom of each languages/*.rs file (Java, Swift, CSS all do this) and test queries by parsing with a local Parser, running Query::new and QueryCursor, or by calling SemanticExtractor::extract_def_use_for_file for defuse; registration is covered by table tests in languages/mod.rs and lang.rs; integration tests live in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ and use common::call_tool_raw and tempfile::NamedTempFile.
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings (CI: ci.yml lines 135-137, plus -W clippy::cognitive_complexity); workspace lints deny undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used (unwrap/expect allowed in test code via cfg_attr); cargo deny check advisories licenses bans (ci.yml:211); new Cargo.lock entries must be >=7 days old (AGENTS.md); REUSE compliance requires SPDX header on new files.
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option or Vec and never panic: get_node_text() bounds-checks byte ranges and returns None; extract_inheritance returns Vec::new() on wrong node kind (swift.rs:50); query compile errors surface as ParserError::QueryError in parser.rs.

patterns: Each languages/<lang>.rs exposes pub const ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY as r"..." raw strings with a one-line doc comment, plus extract_* handler functions and a #[cfg(test)] module.
LanguageInfo entries in get_language_info() are wired as a match arm per language name; get_ts_language() repeats the grammar constant in a second match.
Element captures use @function for the whole declaration node and a name capture (func_name, method_name, class_name); class-like kinds reuse @class (java.rs, swift.rs, csharp).
Defuse captures are classified by capture-name prefix: write.* is Write, read.* is Read, writeread.* is WriteRead; a Read at an offset already written is dropped (parser_elements.rs:868-890).
Inheritance handlers return prefixed strings such as "extends X" and "implements X" (java.rs), "extends X"/"conforms X" (swift.rs), so the output contract is the prefixed string list.
Grammars without a field for a clause (Swift, PHP) use kind-based child iteration: for i in 0..node.child_count() with child.kind() checks (swift.rs:57-72).
Extension-only languages with no handler (markdown, yaml, css) set most LanguageInfo fields to None or empty; defuse_query: None is the existing opt-out.
Language-name strings are the single key across lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP value, supported_languages) and mod.rs (match arms).

library_findings.notes: Context7 (/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php) confirmed base_clause and class_interface_clause have no field names and that class_declaration fields are only attributes, body, name. Note that variable names are variable_name nodes that wrap a name child, so DEFUSE captures must target (variable_name (name) @...) to match the bare symbol text. Anonymous functions (anonymous_function, arrow_function) are not named declarations and are excluded from ELEMENT_QUERY.

approaches.name: A. Java-mirror handler with LANGUAGE_PHP (recommended)
approaches.description: New languages/php.rs with the five query constants modelled on java.rs (ELEMENT_QUERY with name captures, CALL_QUERY over function/member/scoped calls, REFERENCE_QUERY over base/implements names, IMPORT_QUERY over namespace_use_declaration, DEFUSE_QUERY with write/writeread/read prefixes) plus extract_inheritance walking base_clause and class_interface_clause children by kind. Register "php" in mod.rs (pub mod, get_language_info, get_ts_language) using tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP and in lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages). Add tree-sitter-php to workspace and core Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock; README list; integration test file.
pros: Matches every acceptance criterion in #1864, including the HTML-template edge case, because LANGUAGE_PHP (not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY) accepts text outside <?php tags.
Follows the java.rs / swift.rs contract exactly, so parser.rs, parser_elements.rs and the defuse path need no changes.
Keeps tree-sitter-php's real node kinds (function_definition, method_declaration, base_clause, class_interface_clause) confirmed against node-types.json.
tree-sitter-php dev-dep tree-sitter 0.27 and tree-sitter-language 0.1 already match the workspace (tree-sitter 0.27.x; tree-sitter-language 0.1.9 locked).
cons: Inheritance requires kind-based child iteration because base_clause and class_interface_clause have no field names; slightly more code than Java's field walk.
Element/defuse queries match by name text only (no scope), so same-named symbols in different classes are conflated, as in the other handlers.

Cargo age check: tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 was tagged 2026-11-19 on GitHub (8 days before this run); crates.io publish date must be confirmed to be >=7 days old, otherwise pin 0.25.1 (tagged 2026-10-06).

approaches.name: B. Minimal element-and-inheritance only (DEFUSE_QUERY omitted)
approaches.description: Ship php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY and extract_inheritance only; set CALL_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY to empty strings and defuse_query: None in mod.rs, mirroring markdown/yaml/css which set defuse_query: None.
pros: Smallest diff and lowest risk; fewer queries to validate.
Matches the existing pattern for markdown, yaml, css and fortran, which leave defuse_query as None.
cons: Fails acceptance criteria: the issue requires free, -> and :: calls and use imports in analyze_file output.
Symbol-level def-use returns nothing for PHP: parser_elements.rs returns vec![] when compiled.defuse is None, so the def-use tooling silently yields no sites for PHP files.
Leaves a known gap the maintainers explicitly listed in the scope (five query constants).

approaches.name: C. Upstream tags.scm-derived queries with capture renaming
approaches.description: Start from the grammar's queries/tags.scm (definition.function, definition.class, reference.call, reference.implementation, all keyed by name) and rewrite captures to the names aptu-coder consumes (function, class, class_name, method_name, call, import_path, type_ref), then add DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance as in approach A.
pros: Reuses the grammar maintainers' own symbol vocabulary, which reduces the risk of a wrong node kind.
tags.scm already covers object_creation_expression and property_declaration, which could be added later.
cons: tags.scm uses @definition.* and @reference.* capture names that aptu-coder does not consume, so every capture must be renamed; a mismatch fails silently (no match), not at compile time.
tags.scm has no import query and no defuse query, so the extra work is the same as approach A.
Pulls in object_creation and property captures outside the issue's stated element set.

recommendation: Approach A (Java-mirror handler on LANGUAGE_PHP). It is the only option that satisfies every acceptance criterion in #1864: calls, use imports, HTML-template parsing (LANGUAGE_PHP, not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY), and symbol-level def-use via DEFUSE_QUERY. It reuses the proven java.rs/swift.rs contract, so parser.rs and parser_elements.rs need no changes. Approach B is rejected because it drops calls, imports and def-use. Approach C is a fallback only if the node kinds in the grammar prove unstable, because its capture renaming fails silently. Before coding: confirm the crates.io publish date of tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 against the 7-day age rule (fall back to 0.25.1), and compile the five queries in a unit test first, as the issue's Suggested Approach step 3 says.

element_query_draft:
ELEMENT_QUERY (6 patterns):
(function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(trait_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
Captures: function_definition name field -> @func_name; method_declaration name field -> @method_name; class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration name field -> @class_name; whole declaration node -> @function (functions and methods) or @class (type declarations).
defuse_query_draft:
DEFUSE_QUERY (5 patterns), adapted from java.rs DEFUSE_QUERY (write.local / write.assign / writeread.update / read.usage):
(assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name) @write.assign))
(augmented_assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name) @writeread.augment))
(update_expression argument: (variable_name (name) @writeread.update))
(simple_parameter name: (variable_name (name) @write.param))
(variable_name (name) @read.usage)
Why required: parser.rs compiles defuse_query only when Some; parser_elements.rs find-def-use returns vec![] when compiled.defuse is None, so without this constant symbol-level def-use returns no PHP sites. write.assign covers $x = ...; writeread.augment covers $x += ...; writeread.update covers $x++; write.param covers function parameters (PHP has no local declaration keyword, so simple_parameter is the write site analogous to Java local_variable_declaration); read.usage covers every $x occurrence and is deduplicated against write offsets.
inheritance_walk_citation: Source inspected: common/define-grammar.js (fetched via gh api from tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php, the grammar that php/grammar.js defines) and php/src/node-types.json. (1) class_declaration = prec.right(seq(optional(field('attributes', attribute_list)), repeat(_modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', name)), optional(base_clause), optional(class_interface_clause), field('body', declaration_list))). (2) base_clause = seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1(_name)). (3) class_interface_clause = seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1(_name)). (4) _name = choice(alias(keyword('static')...), alias(CAST_TYPE...), reserved('classes', name), qualified_name, relative_name), so each base or interface name is a node of kind name, qualified_name or relative_name. node-types.json: class_declaration fields are exactly attributes, body, name (no parent_class, base_classes or interfaces field); base_clause and class_interface_clause have empty fields and children [name, qualified_name, relative_name]. Field-by-field walk for extract_inheritance(class_node, source): name = class_node.child_by_field_name("name") (kind name, the class identifier); base list = NOT a field, so iterate class_node children by kind: for child with kind "base_clause", for each named child of kind name|qualified_name|relative_name push format!("extends {text}"); for child with kind "class_interface_clause", for each named child of kind name|qualified_name|relative_name push format!("implements {text}"). Anonymous keyword tokens 'extends' and 'implements' are skipped by named_child iteration. For interface_declaration the extends list is also a base_clause child (interface_declaration children: attribute_list, name field, base_clause optional, declaration_list body), so the same walk yields extends entries for interfaces. enum_declaration may carry class_interface_clause (implements) but no base_clause. Swift's extract_inheritance (swift.rs:49) uses the same kind-based child iteration pattern.
